summary: Runtime parity has four separate surfaces; byte-identical skill roots prove only the first. (1) Skills: .claude/skills and .agents/skills are byte-identical copies; scripts/skill-view-parity.sh checks presence and bytes, and an ignored local __pycache__ under an executed skill script reports a false byte difference. (2) Guidance: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md plus readiness agent-commands projections differ only in target names under .fsgg/agents.yml requireEquivalentClaudeAndCodexBehavior. (3) Subagents: only Claude Code binds .claude/agents fsgg-{worker,critic,analyst}-{best,normal}; tests/skill-quality/agent-definition-coverage.py fixes best=opus high and normal=sonnet high. (4) Model routes: every runtime-specific model statement must name both runtimes. On 2026-10-22 the shared work-board lifecycle contract named only gpt-6-astra/gpt-6.1-sol, leaving a wrapperless Claude Code host without a supported route; it now also names opus high for planning and sonnet high for implementation. When adding a model route, grep skills for runtime model names and check the other runtime is named. Source parity does not prove installed consumer adoption.
title: Claude Code and Codex runtime parity covers skills, guidance, agents and model routes
